title: Historical information
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 7 Social Studies; not yet checked by a CBC Social Studies teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Bring sources: an old photograph, a letter, a textbook page, a recorded story. Sort them by kind and by primary or secondary.

skills.key_step: The child names the sources of historical information and matches each to an example.

floor.question: Name one oral method of traditional education.

steps: Ask: spoken, written, dug up, language, picture?
contexts: old pots dug at a site

board.say: Which example goes here: a fossil or a diary?

misconceptions.ask: Which is a source of history?
misconceptions.repair: Ask where the history of the community was kept before writing.

misconceptions.ask: A fossil and old pots dug from the ground are which source?
misconceptions.repair: Ask: do you hear or dig the evidence?

misconceptions.ask: How can similar words in two languages give historical information?
misconceptions.repair: Compare a few shared words in two Bantu languages.

misconceptions.ask: What can a fossil tell historians?
misconceptions.repair: Show a fossil photo with the bone shape visible.

checks.question: Give two sources of historical information.
checks.answer: any two of: oral traditions, written records, archaeology, language, genealogies, photographs, audio-visual records

checks.question: Old pots dug from the ground are which source?

skills.key_step: The child tells primary sources (made at the time by someone there) from secondary sources (made later).

floor.question: Give one source of history.
floor.answer: any source such as oral tradition

representations: the test question: was the maker there?

misconceptions.ask: A textbook written in 2024 about the 1884 Berlin Conference is which source?
misconceptions.repair: Ask whether the author was at the conference.

misconceptions.ask: A diary a soldier wrote during the First World War is which source?
misconceptions.repair: Ask who wrote the diary and when.

misconceptions.ask: You interview your grandmother about her own wedding in 1970. What kind of source is it?
A documentary made in 2020 about independence in 1963. Primary or secondary?
misconceptions.repair: Ask who made it and when.

checks.question: A letter written during the First World War by a soldier is which source?
A textbook written today about the past is which source?

skills.key_step: The child says how historical information has been kept over the years.
steps: Say how it was kept long ago.
Say how it is kept today.

board.say: How was oral history kept long ago?

board.do: Write how it is kept today.

misconceptions.ask: How has oral history been kept?
misconceptions.repair: Ask how a grandmother passes on a proverb.

misconceptions.ask: How are old objects best preserved?
misconceptions.repair: Ask what rain and sun do to old paper.
Show the Kenya National Archives photo.

misconceptions.ask: How can a phone help keep history?
misconceptions.repair: Record a short story from an elder.

checks.question: How has oral history been kept?
checks.answer: in songs, proverbs and stories, and now by recording

checks.question: Where are old objects best kept?
